title: Paramartha Guru Tale 76
summary: After eating three bowls of cold curd rice seasoned with mustard seeds, Guru Paramartha fell into an unusually deep, heavy afternoon slum...
full_text:
After eating three bowls of cold curd rice seasoned with mustard seeds, Guru Paramartha fell into an unusually deep, heavy afternoon slumber on his veranda cot. His breathing was so slow and shallow that his belly scarcely moved, and his limbs felt cold to the touch.

Matti approached to awaken him for evening prayers: 'Master! Master!'

The Guru did not stir.

Matti pinched his ear; the Guru merely snored softly.

Matti shrieked in hysterical grief: 'AI-YO! DISASTER! OUR MASTER HAS DEPARTED FOR THE OTHER WORLD! HE IS NO MORE!'

The five disciples gathered around the cot, beating their chests and wailing in chorus: 'OH, OUR REVERED PRECEPTOR! THE SUN OF PHILOSOPHY HAS SET!'

Madayan examined the Guru's cold toes and consulted an ancient palm-leaf manuscript: 'According to the treatise on clinical expiration: "When the limbs are cold as clay and the eyes remain shut against loud weeping, the soul has dissolved its connection to the physical vessel!" The Master is officially, philosophically deceased! We must conduct the funeral procession before the stars turn inauspicious!'

The disciples built a bamboo funeral bier, laid the sleeping Guru upon it, tied him securely with straw cords, and covered him with white cotton cloths, showering his beard with yellow marigold petals.

Lifting the heavy bier upon their shoulders, the five disciples marched toward the village cremation ground, chanting mournfully: 'GOVINDA! GOVINDA! THE MASTER HAS EMBARKED UPON HIS CELESTIAL JOURNEY!'

The bumpy, swinging motion of the bier, the loud shouting of the disciples, and the afternoon breeze gradually awakened Guru Paramartha from his deep sleep.

He opened his eyes, smelled the marigolds, felt the straw ropes binding his arms, and saw the treetops swinging past above his head!

Sitting up on the bier, the bewildered Guru shouted: 'WHAT IS THIS? WHERE ARE YOU CARRYING ME?'

Matti, marching at the front, looked back over his shoulder and shrieked in terror: 'MASTER! DO NOT SPEAK! YOU ARE DECEASED! THE SCRIPTURE SAYS YOU ARE DEAD!'

The Guru roared: 'You fool! I am alive! Untie these ropes and put me down!'

Madayan reprimanded his master with scholarly severity: 'Revered Master, it is unseemly for a great philosopher to dispute his own medical diagnosis! You exhibited every clinical symptom of mortality! A ghost who speaks on his own funeral bier creates dreadful civic confusion! Lie down and accept your dissolution with dignity!'

The Guru struggled against the straw ropes, shouting: 'I AM NOT A GHOST! I AM HUNGRY! I WANT RICE!'

As they passed the village pond, where several washermen were beating laundry, the Guru shouted to them: 'HELP! MY OWN DISCIPLES ARE CARRYING ME TO THE CREMATION FIRE!'

The washermen dropped their clothes, ran to the road, and stopped the procession.

The chief washerman cut the straw ropes with his knife: 'He is breathing, shouting, and red-faced! He is completely alive, you madmen!'

Guru Paramartha scrambled off the bier, seized a heavy bamboo stick from the litter, and chased his five disciples across the fields, shouting: 'I will demonstrate how alive I am upon your shoulders!'

Madayan, running for his life, called back: 'A magnificent physiological resurrection, Master! Our funeral procession was therapeutic!'
moral: Believing a medical formula over living breath conducts a funeral for the breathing.
